Freedom of speech is not the freedom to exploit others. Voat stands passionately for freedom of speech, but it also has three sitewide rules that exist for good reason: no spam, no illegal content, no doxxing.

Illegal content usually refers to child pornagraphy -- content which by nature exploits children. Doxxing involves the association of intended anonymous internet accounts with real-world identities, potentially putting those real people in dangerous situations. Spam floods the platform of content with one specific message or domain, making it so that other voices have serious difficulty being heard -- it is the equivalent of trigglypuff showing up at every public speaking event and REEEEEing until the speaker goes away. All of these actions exploit other people, and thus go beyond the realm of individual freedom by intervening with others' freedom.

This is why accounts have received sitewide bans from Voat for spamming, for doxxing, and even for vote manipulation (a different kind of content exploitation); there have not been any bans for illegal content, fortunately, at least since February when I started keeping track and Putt made the announcement that he would be cracking down on these things.
